title: Make the emulation FI story a CI gate: nightly rainbow sweeps over fsbl::verify_images, cmd_fw_commit + staging window, confirm/chord gate and the real c10 signer with the correlated-fault model, plus an ELF-level check that double-read/compare sequences survived LTO
threat: A green tree says nothing about FI regressions since the last manual sweep: ci.yml has no rainbow step, the full C10 sweep was only smoke-run, the harness c10 target signs twice with plain sk.sign (no F-16 independent shuffle), the correlated-fault class (same deterministic HASH/position fault in both passes) is unmodelled, and TF-M's documented hazard — the compiler folding redundant reads under -Os/LTO — has only a local fi_min IR check that is not in invariant-gates.
proposal: (1) Add a nightly CI job (self-hosted runner, time-boxed) running tools/sca fault_sweep_* under the three single-fault models + two-fault, publishing the SECURE/INSECURE map as an artifact and failing on any new INSECURE site vs a committed baseline (fi_check style). (2) New targets: fsbl::verify_images + filter_valid (#591), cmd_fw_commit + staging BEGIN→CHUNK→COMMIT (#633), confirm_checked + px chord arming (#211), batch member loop (#335). (3) Correlated-fault mode: inject the identical fault at the identical hash-call index in both sign passes, with and without the F-16 shuffle seeds, and assert ct_eq catches it only when seeds differ (#592/#296). (4) Disassembly gate over the release secure ELF and FSBL ELF: for each `check_true*`, `read_volatile_voted`, FihBool double-read and ct_eq site, assert the expected volatile load/compare count is present (objdump + a small script), added to `make invariant-gates` with check-fi-ir. (5) Retain sweep receipts in-tree so CLAUDE.md claims are auditable.
rationale: Ledger ships exactly this workflow (rainbow + fi_check in CI mapping hits to source) and TF-M explicitly warns that optimisation removes FIH code; it is cheaper than the on-silicon gates and is the regression net for every other item here.

vendor_precedent: Ledger Donjon rainbow fault_skip/fault_stuck_at + fi_check in CI (blog 'fault-injection-simulation'); TF-M FIH design doc (compiler-elimination warning, simulated skip list for SAU/MPC/PSP-limit/NS-entry).
risks: ~40 h host compute for the full C10 sweep — needs sharding or a reduced per-night subset with the full sweep weekly; emulation cannot find unmodelled effects (Ledger's own caveat), so it complements FI-01, not replaces it. Baseline-diff gating can be gamed by moving a site; review the baseline on every change.
